author: runtime_evidence
source_context: Uncommitted D2 working tree with concurrent, separately owned main-agent changes. Head alone is not the tested source. Draft replays replace only the named module(s) in an isolated Python process.
aggregation_policy: Runs overlap. Do not add these pass/fail counts into a unique total or describe draft mechanism defects as failures of the old release. No research efficiency or scientific outcome gain is measured.

limitations: Catalog/claim DB fields are routing metadata, not capabilities. Native lifecycle authority is read from the exact existing database.

Ordinary admission uses mode=ro and does not create/migrate a DB. Explicit matching effect lease plus a caller-owned Lake transaction uses that connection to see its just-closed uncommitted attempt; it does not commit or roll back the caller.
Absence of all routes retains legacy compatibility. This slice does not implement startup or resume recovery.

coverage: Real native training confirmed graceful kill and config-free atexit close generic attempt/lifecycle with precise compute receipts.
False stop, SQL RAISE(IGNORE), and commit failure preserve handle and durable stop/effect HOLD.
Missing route DB and wrong scope/reference do not stop a process or create a DB.
Graceful native training detach preserves claim, process identity, start receipt and RUNNING attempt; it does not claim a successful resume.
Connection close error does not erase an already verified terminal or pretend rollback; handle remains and cleanup returns without aborting other work.
limitations: The main agent's four native evaluation shutdown reds are separate evidence, not newly reproduced old-release failures here.
No startup recovery implementation was assessed. Persisted detach ownership is not proof that a fresh controller can reconstruct or resume the process.
This slice does not fence external worker writes to canonical artifacts or add recovery for unresolved HOLD.
